response.summary_plain: JPL's Small-Body Database has no asteroid or comet matching “Notaname Zzq”. Try a number (433), a name (Eros) or a designation (2024 YR4).
response.why_it_matters_plain: Old images that happen to show a known object are called precovery observations. Each one adds a position at a new date, which lengthens the stretch of time over which an asteroid or comet has been observed. A longer observed arc pins down the orbit, so future positions can be predicted more precisely. The frames below are where SPHEREx's images should contain an asteroid or comet, according to JPL's current orbit.
